item.title: NOTICE OF RATIFICATION OF A MINOR RULES VIOLATION
item.description:
Probation | Special Materials | Notice | Flagged: Special Materials (non-routine) In plain English (machine-written): The Department of Probation's chief procurement officer ratified a procedural violation on Nov. 18, 2026, in a negotiated extension of the NYCHA Neighborhood Employment Services Program contract with Center for Employment Opportunities, Inc., because public notice ran after the March 1, 2025 start date.

On November 18, 2026, pursuant to Section 1-02(h)(1)(ii) of the New York City Procurement Policy Board (PPB) Rules, the City Chief Procurement Officer (CCPO) ratified a Minor Rules Violation request submitted by the New York City Department of Probation (DOP) in connection with the Negotiated Acquisition Extension (NAE) for the NYCHA Neighborhood Employment Services Program.

The violation concerned compliance with PPB Rule §2-11, as the public notice and comment process was conducted after the proposed contract commencement date of March 1, 2025. The public notice was published on April 16, 2026, with comments accepted through April 29, 2026. DOP also republished the Notice of Intent to reflect the revised contract term and amount.

DOP determined that the procedural violation had no significant adverse impact on the procurement process or its intended outcome, and that ratification is in the best interests of the City. The ratification allows DOP to proceed with the remaining contract approval and registration requirements.

item.title: Facility Maintenance Information System
item.description:
NYC Health + Hospitals | Procurement | Solicitation | Due: 2026-12-28 | Flagged: Sole-source / non-competitive In plain English (machine-written): NYC Health + Hospitals is seeking proposals from vendors to buy and set up a new facilities management and asset information system to track and manage its buildings and infrastructure, with responses due Dec. 28, 2026.

NYC Health + Hospitals consists of buildings and infrastructure of various ages and conditions across its many campuses. As the patient base has increased and the methods of delivering care has changed, the buildings, many of which are decades old, have to be constantly upgraded or replaced. This growth has driven the growth of the total square feet of the system to be maintained to over 20,000,000 sq. ft. The Office of Facilities Development (OFD) is responsible for maintenance and operations of all campuses and buildings to ensure the clinicians have the facilities needed to deliver care. Campuses within the network range in size from a few thousand to over a 1 million square feet emphasizing the need for a new and robust Facilities Management and Asset Information System (FMIS) with the capability and capacity to organize, identify, and manage all infrastructure assets. This project entails the procurement and implementation of an industry-standard FMIS solution that will fulfill the business requirements of the Health System.
